node: Regulated utilities and LNG/oil-gas infrastructure capex
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Expanded the direct public-company universe around regulated utility and LNG/oil-gas infrastructure capex. The highest-signal underfollowed lane is not regulated utilities themselves, but suppliers and contractors that sit one step upstream of utility, transmission, LNG, midstream, and power-generation capex: engineered electrical distribution systems, transmission-line hardware, utility/LNG EPC services, and specialty infrastructure construction. This pass is research-only and does not imply any buy/sell view. Expanded the universe around regulated utility and LNG/oil-gas infrastructure capex with a deliberate bias toward second-order suppliers rather than obvious utilities or mega-cap electrical equipment leaders. The strongest underfollowed candidates in this pass sit in transmission hardware, packaged electrical power distribution, PVF distribution for gas utilities, and LNG/utility peak-shaving construction. These names are not recommendations; they are Layer 1B research candidates requiring segment-level evidence, backlog checks, customer verification, and margin-cycle falsification in later layers. Layer 1B expanded the universe around regulated utility and LNG/oil-gas capex by separating one high-attention reference contractor from three less obvious supplier/distributor names. The underfollowed lane emphasizes companies selling enabling hardware, electrical systems, or PVF distribution into utilities, oil/gas, petrochemical, LNG, and energy-transition-adjacent infrastructure. Key chokepoint angle: old-economy utility and hydrocarbon customers can fund recurring cap
